summary: Layer 1B expansion for the nuclear fuel and nuclear-qualified components node identifies one high-attention reference fuel-cycle name and two less obvious discovery-lane names. The most direct public-market exposure remains Centrus Energy because HALEU production, DOE contracts, NRC licensing, and domestic enrichment capacity map tightly to the bottleneck hypothesis. Curtiss-Wright is a less obvious large-cap industrial/defense supplier with nuclear-qualified reactor coolant pumps, control rod drive mechanisms, severe-service valves, heat-exchanger repair, and test/isolation services. ASP Isotopes is a small-cap speculative shadow candidate through Quantum Leap Energy's stated HALEU and advanced nuclear fuel ambitions, but evidence quality is materially weaker and requires later verification of uranium enrichment technology, licensing, financing, customer contracts, and dilution risk.
